# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1445
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1445
- **Title**: gh-1441 Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1441` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +1276
- **Deletions**: -3
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:45:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T18:53:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #1441
### Root Cause

`voxel` nodes render the "Voxel world" placeholder because the Fa app built `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both construction sites — the fullscreen view (`js_app_view.dart` `_treeView`) and the live tile (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`). The runtime falls back to the `Icons.landscape` placeholder exactly when the world is null, so `fa-craft`/`voxel-sandbox` resolved their `voxel.*` probes and uploaded meshes while the screen showed the placeholder (exposed by the gh-1341 `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, which made the widgets' probes resolve).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`: expose `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` — always the CURRENT engine's bridge-owned world (null before start / after dispose, so a reload re-wires, never a stale world). Plus `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld(tree)`: a one-shot `AppLog` diagnostic so a null world on a voxel tree reads as "host wiring", not "broken widget".
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`: pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` (mirrors the existing `webViewHost`/`js3dHost` wiring) + the diagnostic call.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart`: same wiring in `DynamicWidgetCanvas`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/jsr_voxel_world_pin_guard_test.dart` (REG-1): static guard asserting every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` in both surfaces passes `voxelWorld:` and the getter delegates to `_engine` — **failed before the fix** (reproduction), blocks merge even when widget tests skip.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_engine_voxel_world_test.dart` (UT-1/AC5+AC3): world identity across restart, null before start/after dispose; one-shot diagnostic asserted via `AppLog.dump()`; null-world placeholder still renders without crash.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_view_voxel_test.dart` (IT-1/AC1+E1): real-engine boot through `JsAppView` — `JsVoxelNode` present, placeholder absent; bare first-tree voxel node (zero `voxel.*` calls) renders via the eager bridge world.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/dynamic_widget_tile_voxel_test.dart` (IT-2/AC2): same assertions through the tile canvas.
- Engine-dependent legs gated on `quickJsBridgeAvailable` (repo pattern): live-verified on Linux QuickJS (`LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`), run on the CI macOS exzone leg, skip on bare ubuntu.
- Regression sweep on this runner: `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` → **543 passed, 0 failed** (the CI exzone surface, engines live); the diff's importing suites (`test/golden`, `app_launcher_screen_test`, `chat_screen_test`, `analytics_guard_test`) → 41 passed; full `flutter_app` suite failures (222) are byte-identical on the pre-fix baseline commit and confined to the host-locked golden suite (220 — documented ubuntu-excluded in `ci.yml`) plus 2 env-bound legs (wasm shell scripting, OAuth port binding) in suites this diff never touches. `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`: no issues in changed files.

### Notes

- Degradation contract (AC3) kept: a world-less engine still renders the renderer's placeholder; shipped backends always have a world, so the diagnostic never fires there.
- AC4 catalog-app E2E goldens (`fa-craft`, `voxel-sandbox`) are not executable in this runner — the fixtures live in the remote catalog; the IT tests replicate their exact probe → upload → camera protocol instead.
- REG-2 backend parity: the getter is backend-agnostic; the live-world leg covers the native flutter_js backend (QuickJS here, JSC on macOS CI). The web-worker backend is upstream-owned and not loadable in `flutter_test` on this runner.

blocks.text:
**Root cause of the CRAP gate failure:** `CRAP threshold exceeded: 90.00 > 30.0`.

Some function in `flutter_app` (per `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml` scope) has CRAP score 90 (max threshold 30). CRAP = comp+¹ × coverage-weighted. A CRAP of 90 means a complex, UNCOVERED function. My change touched only a test file — tests don't enter the crap scope (lib scope). The previous pass added code to `js_app_engine.dart` (`_containsVoxelNode` recursion, `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld`) and `apps_golden_test.dart`... but lib files are the scope.

Which function has CRAP 90? The CI ratchet doesn't name it in this tail — let me run crap4dart locally to find it. The CRAP gate measures coverage-weighted crap: the CI merges app-coverage shards and computes. My local run can reproduce: `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` needs the coverage lcov at flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info presumably.

Which function could be at 90? `_containsVoxelNode` in js_app_engine.dart — complexity: if/else-if, loops, recursion... CRAP = crap(comp, coverage) = comp² + comp×(1−coverage). # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1445
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1445
- **Title**: gh-1441 Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1441` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +1276
- **Deletions**: -3
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:45:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T18:53:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #1441
### Root Cause

`voxel` nodes render the "Voxel world" placeholder because the Fa app built `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both construction sites — the fullscreen view (`js_app_view.dart` `_treeView`) and the live tile (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`). The runtime falls back to the `Icons.landscape` placeholder exactly when the world is null, so `fa-craft`/`voxel-sandbox` resolved their `voxel.*` probes and uploaded meshes while the screen showed the placeholder (exposed by the gh-1341 `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, which made the widgets' probes resolve).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`: expose `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` — always the CURRENT engine's bridge-owned world (null before start / after dispose, so a reload re-wires, never a stale world). Plus `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld(tree)`: a one-shot `AppLog` diagnostic so a null world on a voxel tree reads as "host wiring", not "broken widget".
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`: pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` (mirrors the existing `webViewHost`/`js3dHost` wiring) + the diagnostic call.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart`: same wiring in `DynamicWidgetCanvas`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/jsr_voxel_world_pin_guard_test.dart` (REG-1): static guard asserting every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` in both surfaces passes `voxelWorld:` and the getter delegates to `_engine` — **failed before the fix** (reproduction), blocks merge even when widget tests skip.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_engine_voxel_world_test.dart` (UT-1/AC5+AC3): world identity across restart, null before start/after dispose; one-shot diagnostic asserted via `AppLog.dump()`; null-world placeholder still renders without crash.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_view_voxel_test.dart` (IT-1/AC1+E1): real-engine boot through `JsAppView` — `JsVoxelNode` present, placeholder absent; bare first-tree voxel node (zero `voxel.*` calls) renders via the eager bridge world.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/dynamic_widget_tile_voxel_test.dart` (IT-2/AC2): same assertions through the tile canvas.
- Engine-dependent legs gated on `quickJsBridgeAvailable` (repo pattern): live-verified on Linux QuickJS (`LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`), run on the CI macOS exzone leg, skip on bare ubuntu.
- Regression sweep on this runner: `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` → **543 passed, 0 failed** (the CI exzone surface, engines live); the diff's importing suites (`test/golden`, `app_launcher_screen_test`, `chat_screen_test`, `analytics_guard_test`) → 41 passed; full `flutter_app` suite failures (222) are byte-identical on the pre-fix baseline commit and confined to the host-locked golden suite (220 — documented ubuntu-excluded in `ci.yml`) plus 2 env-bound legs (wasm shell scripting, OAuth port binding) in suites this diff never touches. `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`: no issues in changed files.

### Notes

- Degradation contract (AC3) kept: a world-less engine still renders the renderer's placeholder; shipped backends always have a world, so the diagnostic never fires there.
- AC4 catalog-app E2E goldens (`fa-craft`, `voxel-sandbox`) are not executable in this runner — the fixtures live in the remote catalog; the IT tests replicate their exact probe → upload → camera protocol instead.
- REG-2 backend parity: the getter is backend-agnostic; the live-world leg covers the native flutter_js backend (QuickJS here, JSC on macOS CI). The web-worker backend is upstream-owned and not loadable in `flutter_test` on this runner.

My change touched only a test file — tests don't enter the crap scope (lib scope). The previous pass added code to `js_app_engine.dart` (`_containsVoxelNode` recursion, `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld`) and `apps_golden_test.dart`... but lib files are the scope.

Which function has CRAP 90? The CI ratchet doesn't name it in this tail — let me run crap4dart locally to find it. The CRAP gate measures coverage-weighted crap: the CI merges app-coverage shards and computes. My local run can reproduce: `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` needs the coverage lcov at flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info presumably.

Which function could be at 90? `_containsVoxelNode` in js_app_engine.dart — complexity: if/else-if, loops, recursion... CRAP = crap(comp, coverage) = comp² + comp×(1−coverage). If comp ~9 and coverage 0 → 90. comp 9 ≈ 8 decision points + 1. `_containsVoxelNode`: `depth > 64` (1), `is Map` (2), `== 'voxel'` (3), for loop (4), `is List` (5), for loop (6) → comp 7 → 7²=49+7×(1−cov). With cov 0 → 56. Hmm not 90.

`maskedForScan`? That's in ROOT test/ — flutter_app scope only covers flutter_app/lib. The 90 could be a function in flutter_app/lib with the merged coverage from the 2 shards. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1445
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1445
- **Title**: gh-1441 Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1441` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +1276
- **Deletions**: -3
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:45:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T18:53:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #1441
### Root Cause

`voxel` nodes render the "Voxel world" placeholder because the Fa app built `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both construction sites — the fullscreen view (`js_app_view.dart` `_treeView`) and the live tile (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`). The runtime falls back to the `Icons.landscape` placeholder exactly when the world is null, so `fa-craft`/`voxel-sandbox` resolved their `voxel.*` probes and uploaded meshes while the screen showed the placeholder (exposed by the gh-1341 `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, which made the widgets' probes resolve).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`: expose `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` — always the CURRENT engine's bridge-owned world (null before start / after dispose, so a reload re-wires, never a stale world). Plus `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld(tree)`: a one-shot `AppLog` diagnostic so a null world on a voxel tree reads as "host wiring", not "broken widget".
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`: pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` (mirrors the existing `webViewHost`/`js3dHost` wiring) + the diagnostic call.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart`: same wiring in `DynamicWidgetCanvas`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/jsr_voxel_world_pin_guard_test.dart` (REG-1): static guard asserting every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` in both surfaces passes `voxelWorld:` and the getter delegates to `_engine` — **failed before the fix** (reproduction), blocks merge even when widget tests skip.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_engine_voxel_world_test.dart` (UT-1/AC5+AC3): world identity across restart, null before start/after dispose; one-shot diagnostic asserted via `AppLog.dump()`; null-world placeholder still renders without crash.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_view_voxel_test.dart` (IT-1/AC1+E1): real-engine boot through `JsAppView` — `JsVoxelNode` present, placeholder absent; bare first-tree voxel node (zero `voxel.*` calls) renders via the eager bridge world.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/dynamic_widget_tile_voxel_test.dart` (IT-2/AC2): same assertions through the tile canvas.
- Engine-dependent legs gated on `quickJsBridgeAvailable` (repo pattern): live-verified on Linux QuickJS (`LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`), run on the CI macOS exzone leg, skip on bare ubuntu.
- Regression sweep on this runner: `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` → **543 passed, 0 failed** (the CI exzone surface, engines live); the diff's importing suites (`test/golden`, `app_launcher_screen_test`, `chat_screen_test`, `analytics_guard_test`) → 41 passed; full `flutter_app` suite failures (222) are byte-identical on the pre-fix baseline commit and confined to the host-locked golden suite (220 — documented ubuntu-excluded in `ci.yml`) plus 2 env-bound legs (wasm shell scripting, OAuth port binding) in suites this diff never touches. `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`: no issues in changed files.

### Notes

- Degradation contract (AC3) kept: a world-less engine still renders the renderer's placeholder; shipped backends always have a world, so the diagnostic never fires there.
- AC4 catalog-app E2E goldens (`fa-craft`, `voxel-sandbox`) are not executable in this runner — the fixtures live in the remote catalog; the IT tests replicate their exact probe → upload → camera protocol instead.
- REG-2 backend parity: the getter is backend-agnostic; the live-world leg covers the native flutter_js backend (QuickJS here, JSC on macOS CI). The web-worker backend is upstream-owned and not loadable in `flutter_test` on this runner.

**Root cause of the CRAP gate failure:** `CRAP threshold exceeded: 90.00 > 30.0`.

Some function in `flutter_app` (per `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml` scope) has CRAP score 90 (max threshold 30). CRAP = comp+¹ × coverage-weighted. A CRAP of 90 means a complex, UNCOVERED function. My change touched only a test file — tests don't enter the crap scope (lib scope). The previous pass added code to `js_app_engine.dart` (`_containsVoxelNode` recursion, `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld`) and `apps_golden_test.dart`... but lib files are the scope.

Which function has CRAP 90? The CI ratchet doesn't name it in this tail — let me run crap4dart locally to find it. The CRAP gate measures coverage-weighted crap: the CI merges app-coverage shards and computes. My local run can reproduce: `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` needs the coverage lcov at flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info presumably.

Which function could be at 90? `_containsVoxelNode` in js_app_engine.dart — complexity: if/else-if, loops, recursion... CRAP = crap(comp, coverage) = comp² + comp×(1−coverage). If comp ~9 and coverage 0 → 90. comp 9 ≈ 8 decision points + 1. `_containsVoxelNode`: `depth > 64` (1), `is Map` (2), `== 'voxel'` (3), for loop (4), `is List` (5), for loop (6) → comp 7 → 7²=49+7×(1−cov). With cov 0 → 56. Hmm not 90.

`maskedForScan`? That's in ROOT test/ — flutter_app scope only covers flutter_app/lib. The 90 could be a function in flutter_app/lib with the merged coverage from the 2 shards. Wait — which functions did this PR add to flutter_app/lib? `voxelWorld` getter (comp 1), `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld` (comp ~5), `_containsVoxelNode` (comp 7). None hit 90 unless uncovered with higher comp.

Hold on — the CRAP ratchet compares against a BASELINE (`.crap-baseline.json` at repo root, `crap4dart.yaml` + `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`). "CRAP threshold exceeded: 90.00 > 30.0" — the gate reports the WORST offender. The ratchet baseline should hold known offenders. If a NEW function exceeded 30 (uncovered by the CI shards), the gate fails.

Key: the CI coverage shards come from "Flutter app tests (shard 0/2, 1/2)" — which run the full flutter_app test suite? If the coverage suite doesn't execute `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld`/`_containsVoxelNode` (engine-gated tests SKIP on bare ubuntu CI shards — "skip on bare ubuntu"!), those functions have ZERO coverage → CRAP = comp² + comp.

`_containsVoxelNode`: comp 7 → 49+7 = 56. Not 90. What about the golden test's `addVoxel`? It's in test/ — not in scope (flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml scope is probably flutter_app/lib; and the loc-scope companion covers test/example for LOC only).

# crap4dart configuration for the flutter_app package.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET (issue #433): the threshold is pinned at the CURRENT worst score
# measured by the SAME pipeline the CI gate uses — `flutter test --coverage`
# lcov (E2: widget-test coverage differs from the core's dart lcov, so the
# number must come from this pipeline, not the core's).
# Bootstrap (2026-09-15): 2450.0 — `JsAppEngine._faCall` (CC 49, 0% line
# coverage). Descent #1 (same day): the issue's three named offenders went
# under the next milestone line (CRAP ≤ 40 each) and the threshold followed
# the measured new worst: 2450.0 → 870.0 (`wasm_shell_git.run` and
# `main`, CC 29 at 0% coverage). Descent #2 (issue #475): both beasts
# decomposed into route-table dispatch + per-family handlers with a 51-test
# golden suite, and the cluster's own 812/702/600/506 beasts went down with
# them; the threshold follows the new measured worst: 870.0 → 650.0
# (`runCodemieSsoFlow`, CC 25 at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card).
# Descent #9 (issue #485): the on-device provider stream functions moved to
# one shared pump + codec walk (lib/on_device/), and the beasts went down
# with them — gemma 992 → 9, transformers.js 552/506 → 17/1, webllm 420 → 6
# (all fully covered by the provider suites + the new codec-table/pump
# tests); the threshold follows the measured new worst: 650.0 → 380.0
# (`WasiSandboxShell._runStage`, CC 19 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell cluster,
# another lane's ladder card).
# Pushes may only make the codebase BETTER,
# never worse; scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down rejects a raised
# threshold in CI. The staged ladder continues in follow-up cards:
# 870 → … → 40 (see AGENTS.md "Quality gates"). Re-measure after each fix:
# cd flutter_app && flutter test --coverage &&
# dart pub global run crap4dart analyze.

sources: [lib]

# Same generated set as the root config (E1 parity — asserted by
# scripts/check_crap_guards.py).
exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in flutter_app/lib under the flutter lcov
  # pipeline. Descent #10 (issue #558): the wasm_shell pipeline-engine
  # cluster went down (_runStage 380→4, _runPipeline 210→4, _evalExpr
  # 182→3, _rewriteRelativeArgs 110→2, _maybeRewritePath 72→3, all 100%
  # covered by test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows
  # the measured new worst: 380.0 → 272.0 (`WasiSandboxShell._xargsBuiltin`,
  # CC 16 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell builtins cluster, the next lane's
  # ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #11 (issue #559): the wasm_shell builtins cluster went down
  # (xargs 272→7, _parsePrimary 210→3, _testBuiltin 132→9, du 132→3,
  # tac 90→6, tr 25.9→4, pip 72→3, _expandTrSet 30.8→gone — table/spec
  # driven parse helpers now live in wasm_shell_builtins.dart with direct
  # unit tests, the exec halves are covered e2e in
  # test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows the
  # measured new worst: 272.0 → 210.0 (`GemmaService.chatStream`, CC 14
  # at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #12 (issue #701): the 0%-coverage trio went down (_statBuiltin
  # 156→12.1 @ 91% cov via test/wasm_shell_stat_test.dart, isFaCliInstalled
  # 110→6 via the extracted faCliProbe seam + test/sessions_root_test.dart,
  # _showAppMenu 90→9 @ 100% cov via test/apps/apps_panel_menu_test.dart);
  # the threshold follows the measured new worst: 210.0 → 30.0 (the CC-5
  # 0%-cov tier: routeExtHostMessage, codemie _createController, attached
  # _AttachedRow.build, GemmaService.loadModel — the next ladder cards).
  # Re-measured on the CI pipeline (app-crap-gate run 35479048998): local
  # lcov is impossible on the agent cube (the flutter coverage collector
  # canonicalizes source paths and lstat EPERMs through .worktrees). Only
  # down.
  # TEMP raise (owner call 2026-09-26, mirrors dmtools-dart #256): the #955
  # network-mode merge shipped widgets without tests — max CRAP 72.0
  # (_ChannelRailState._createChannel, CC 8 @ 0% cov). Restore to 30.0 via
  # the linked issue.
  # raise-issue: gh-992
  # Restored (gh-992, 2026-09-27): the agents/enroll DAP-tab rework
  # (fcd2d0232) covered the #955 network UI — 5 enroll dialog groups +
  # channel_rail/chat_page call-site suites, 72 focused tests; re-measured
  # on the full local flutter lcov (3292 green): max CRAP 30.0, the
  # threshold follows back down 75.0 → 30.0. Only down.
  threshold: 30.0

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1445
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1445
- **Title**: gh-1441 Voxel nodes render as the “Voxel world” placeholder — Fa app builds JsonWidgetRenderer without voxelWorld (fa-craft 0.2.18, voxel-sandbox 1.0.0)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1441` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 11
- **Additions**: +1276
- **Deletions**: -3
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:45:40Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T18:53:50Z

## PR Description

Closes #1441
### Root Cause

`voxel` nodes render the "Voxel world" placeholder because the Fa app built `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both construction sites — the fullscreen view (`js_app_view.dart` `_treeView`) and the live tile (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`). The runtime falls back to the `Icons.landscape` placeholder exactly when the world is null, so `fa-craft`/`voxel-sandbox` resolved their `voxel.*` probes and uploaded meshes while the screen showed the placeholder (exposed by the gh-1341 `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, which made the widgets' probes resolve).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`: expose `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` — always the CURRENT engine's bridge-owned world (null before start / after dispose, so a reload re-wires, never a stale world). Plus `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld(tree)`: a one-shot `AppLog` diagnostic so a null world on a voxel tree reads as "host wiring", not "broken widget".
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`: pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` (mirrors the existing `webViewHost`/`js3dHost` wiring) + the diagnostic call.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart`: same wiring in `DynamicWidgetCanvas`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/jsr_voxel_world_pin_guard_test.dart` (REG-1): static guard asserting every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` in both surfaces passes `voxelWorld:` and the getter delegates to `_engine` — **failed before the fix** (reproduction), blocks merge even when widget tests skip.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_engine_voxel_world_test.dart` (UT-1/AC5+AC3): world identity across restart, null before start/after dispose; one-shot diagnostic asserted via `AppLog.dump()`; null-world placeholder still renders without crash.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_view_voxel_test.dart` (IT-1/AC1+E1): real-engine boot through `JsAppView` — `JsVoxelNode` present, placeholder absent; bare first-tree voxel node (zero `voxel.*` calls) renders via the eager bridge world.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/dynamic_widget_tile_voxel_test.dart` (IT-2/AC2): same assertions through the tile canvas.
- Engine-dependent legs gated on `quickJsBridgeAvailable` (repo pattern): live-verified on Linux QuickJS (`LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`), run on the CI macOS exzone leg, skip on bare ubuntu.
- Regression sweep on this runner: `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` → **543 passed, 0 failed** (the CI exzone surface, engines live); the diff's importing suites (`test/golden`, `app_launcher_screen_test`, `chat_screen_test`, `analytics_guard_test`) → 41 passed; full `flutter_app` suite failures (222) are byte-identical on the pre-fix baseline commit and confined to the host-locked golden suite (220 — documented ubuntu-excluded in `ci.yml`) plus 2 env-bound legs (wasm shell scripting, OAuth port binding) in suites this diff never touches. `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`: no issues in changed files.

### Notes

- Degradation contract (AC3) kept: a world-less engine still renders the renderer's placeholder; shipped backends always have a world, so the diagnostic never fires there.
- AC4 catalog-app E2E goldens (`fa-craft`, `voxel-sandbox`) are not executable in this runner — the fixtures live in the remote catalog; the IT tests replicate their exact probe → upload → camera protocol instead.
- REG-2 backend parity: the getter is backend-agnostic; the live-world leg covers the native flutter_js backend (QuickJS here, JSC on macOS CI). The web-worker backend is upstream-owned and not loadable in `flutter_test` on this runner.

blocks.text:
**Root cause of the CRAP gate failure:** `CRAP threshold exceeded: 90.00 > 30.0`.

Some function in `flutter_app` (per `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml` scope) has CRAP score 90 (max threshold 30). CRAP = comp+¹ × coverage-weighted. A CRAP of 90 means a complex, UNCOVERED function. My change touched only a test file — tests don't enter the crap scope (lib scope). The previous pass added code to `js_app_engine.dart` (`_containsVoxelNode` recursion, `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld`) and `apps_golden_test.dart`... but lib files are the scope.

Which function has CRAP 90? The CI ratchet doesn't name it in this tail — let me run crap4dart locally to find it. The CRAP gate measures coverage-weighted crap: the CI merges app-coverage shards and computes. My local run can reproduce: `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` needs the coverage lcov at flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info presumably.

Which function could be at 90? `_containsVoxelNode` in js_app_engine.dart — complexity: if/else-if, loops, recursion... CRAP = crap(comp, coverage) = comp² + comp×(1−coverage). `voxel` nodes render the "Voxel world" placeholder because the Fa app built `JsonWidgetRenderer` **without `voxelWorld`** at both construction sites — the fullscreen view (`js_app_view.dart` `_treeView`) and the live tile (`dynamic_widget_tile.dart`). The runtime falls back to the `Icons.landscape` placeholder exactly when the world is null, so `fa-craft`/`voxel-sandbox` resolved their `voxel.*` probes and uploaded meshes while the screen showed the placeholder (exposed by the gh-1341 `js_widget_runtime` ^0.4.156 pin, which made the widgets' probes resolve).

### Fix

- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`: expose `JsVoxelWorld? get voxelWorld => _engine?.voxelWorld;` — always the CURRENT engine's bridge-owned world (null before start / after dispose, so a reload re-wires, never a stale world). Plus `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld(tree)`: a one-shot `AppLog` diagnostic so a null world on a voxel tree reads as "host wiring", not "broken widget".
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_view.dart`: pass `voxelWorld: engine.voxelWorld` (mirrors the existing `webViewHost`/`js3dHost` wiring) + the diagnostic call.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/dynamic_widget_tile.dart`: same wiring in `DynamicWidgetCanvas`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/jsr_voxel_world_pin_guard_test.dart` (REG-1): static guard asserting every `JsonWidgetRenderer(` in both surfaces passes `voxelWorld:` and the getter delegates to `_engine` — **failed before the fix** (reproduction), blocks merge even when widget tests skip.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_engine_voxel_world_test.dart` (UT-1/AC5+AC3): world identity across restart, null before start/after dispose; one-shot diagnostic asserted via `AppLog.dump()`; null-world placeholder still renders without crash.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/js_app_view_voxel_test.dart` (IT-1/AC1+E1): real-engine boot through `JsAppView` — `JsVoxelNode` present, placeholder absent; bare first-tree voxel node (zero `voxel.*` calls) renders via the eager bridge world.
- `flutter_app/test/apps/dynamic_widget_tile_voxel_test.dart` (IT-2/AC2): same assertions through the tile canvas.
- Engine-dependent legs gated on `quickJsBridgeAvailable` (repo pattern): live-verified on Linux QuickJS (`LIBQUICKJSC_TEST_PATH`), run on the CI macOS exzone leg, skip on bare ubuntu.
- Regression sweep on this runner: `flutter test --exclude-tags integration test/apps` → **543 passed, 0 failed** (the CI exzone surface, engines live); the diff's importing suites (`test/golden`, `app_launcher_screen_test`, `chat_screen_test`, `analytics_guard_test`) → 41 passed; full `flutter_app` suite failures (222) are byte-identical on the pre-fix baseline commit and confined to the host-locked golden suite (220 — documented ubuntu-excluded in `ci.yml`) plus 2 env-bound legs (wasm shell scripting, OAuth port binding) in suites this diff never touches. `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`: no issues in changed files.

### Notes

- Degradation contract (AC3) kept: a world-less engine still renders the renderer's placeholder; shipped backends always have a world, so the diagnostic never fires there.
- AC4 catalog-app E2E goldens (`fa-craft`, `voxel-sandbox`) are not executable in this runner — the fixtures live in the remote catalog; the IT tests replicate their exact probe → upload → camera protocol instead.
- REG-2 backend parity: the getter is backend-agnostic; the live-world leg covers the native flutter_js backend (QuickJS here, JSC on macOS CI). The web-worker backend is upstream-owned and not loadable in `flutter_test` on this runner.

Also note: the "543 passed" claim in the PR description didn't include a CI-crap check — the previous pass never ran the CRAP gate (it's a CI-only gate over merged coverage; pre-commit is core-only).

A. **Reduce complexity + cover it.** `_containsVoxelNode` — make iterative and simpler? CC 9 needs to drop AND/OR get covered. Even CC 5 uncovered = 30 → not >30, passes. CC 5 uncovered → exactly 30.0, threshold check is `> 30.0` → passes. So: reduce CC to ≤5 → gate green even at 0% coverage. # crap4dart configuration for the flutter_app package.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart

blocks.text:
# crap4dart configuration for the flutter_app package.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET (issue #433): the threshold is pinned at the CURRENT worst score
# measured by the SAME pipeline the CI gate uses — `flutter test --coverage`
# lcov (E2: widget-test coverage differs from the core's dart lcov, so the
# number must come from this pipeline, not the core's).
# Bootstrap (2026-09-15): 2450.0 — `JsAppEngine._faCall` (CC 49, 0% line
# coverage). Descent #1 (same day): the issue's three named offenders went
# under the next milestone line (CRAP ≤ 40 each) and the threshold followed
# the measured new worst: 2450.0 → 870.0 (`wasm_shell_git.run` and
# `main`, CC 29 at 0% coverage). Descent #2 (issue #475): both beasts
# decomposed into route-table dispatch + per-family handlers with a 51-test
# golden suite, and the cluster's own 812/702/600/506 beasts went down with
# them; the threshold follows the new measured worst: 870.0 → 650.0
# (`runCodemieSsoFlow`, CC 25 at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card).
# Descent #9 (issue #485): the on-device provider stream functions moved to
# one shared pump + codec walk (lib/on_device/), and the beasts went down
# with them — gemma 992 → 9, transformers.js 552/506 → 17/1, webllm 420 → 6
# (all fully covered by the provider suites + the new codec-table/pump
# tests); the threshold follows the measured new worst: 650.0 → 380.0
# (`WasiSandboxShell._runStage`, CC 19 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell cluster,
# another lane's ladder card).
# Pushes may only make the codebase BETTER,
# never worse; scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down rejects a raised
# threshold in CI. The staged ladder continues in follow-up cards:
# 870 → … → 40 (see AGENTS.md "Quality gates"). Re-measure after each fix:
# cd flutter_app && flutter test --coverage &&
# dart pub global run crap4dart analyze.

sources: [lib]

# Same generated set as the root config (E1 parity — asserted by
# scripts/check_crap_guards.py).
exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in flutter_app/lib under the flutter lcov
  # pipeline. Descent #10 (issue #558): the wasm_shell pipeline-engine
  # cluster went down (_runStage 380→4, _runPipeline 210→4, _evalExpr
  # 182→3, _rewriteRelativeArgs 110→2, _maybeRewritePath 72→3, all 100%
  # covered by test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows
  # the measured new worst: 380.0 → 272.0 (`WasiSandboxShell._xargsBuiltin`,
  # CC 16 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell builtins cluster, the next lane's
  # ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #11 (issue #559): the wasm_shell builtins cluster went down
  # (xargs 272→7, _parsePrimary 210→3, _testBuiltin 132→9, du 132→3,
  # tac 90→6, tr 25.9→4, pip 72→3, _expandTrSet 30.8→gone — table/spec
  # driven parse helpers now live in wasm_shell_builtins.dart with direct
  # unit tests, the exec halves are covered e2e in
  # test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows the
  # measured new worst: 272.0 → 210.0 (`GemmaService.chatStream`, CC 14
  # at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #12 (issue #701): the 0%-coverage trio went down (_statBuiltin
  # 156→12.1 @ 91% cov via test/wasm_shell_stat_test.dart, isFaCliInstalled
  # 110→6 via the extracted faCliProbe seam + test/sessions_root_test.dart,
  # _showAppMenu 90→9 @ 100% cov via test/apps/apps_panel_menu_test.dart);
  # the threshold follows the measured new worst: 210.0 → 30.0 (the CC-5
  # 0%-cov tier: routeExtHostMessage, codemie _createController, attached
  # _AttachedRow.build, GemmaService.loadModel — the next ladder cards).
  # Re-measured on the CI pipeline (app-crap-gate run 35479048998): local
  # lcov is impossible on the agent cube (the flutter coverage collector
  # canonicalizes source paths and lstat EPERMs through .worktrees). Only
  # down.
  # TEMP raise (owner call 2026-09-26, mirrors dmtools-dart #256): the #955
  # network-mode merge shipped widgets without tests — max CRAP 72.0
  # (_ChannelRailState._createChannel, CC 8 @ 0% cov). Restore to 30.0 via
  # the linked issue.
  # raise-issue: gh-992
  # Restored (gh-992, 2026-09-27): the agents/enroll DAP-tab rework
  # (fcd2d0232) covered the #955 network UI — 5 enroll dialog groups +
  # channel_rail/chat_page call-site suites, 72 focused tests; re-measured
  # on the full local flutter lcov (3292 green): max CRAP 30.0, the
  # threshold follows back down 75.0 → 30.0. Only down.
  threshold: 30.0

coverage:
  # The CI app-crap-gate job merges the two flutter-tests shard reports
  # (scripts/merge_lcov.py) right before the CRAP step. Pre-commit stays
  # core-only: flutter coverage is too heavy for every commit.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  # flutter's lcov carries no BRDA branch records; branch coverage stays
  # a core-package gate concern.
  branch_coverage: false
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole flutter suite
  # first. Coverage comes from the CI shard merge (scripts/merge_lcov.py)
  # and pre-commit stays core-only (#433 split); nobody wants a second
  # suite run inside a 6-minute gate job.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This config is the single source of which gates `crap4dart check` runs
# (CI app-crap-gate job, pre-commit core hook): 0.9.5 default-enables ALL
# built-in gates, so everything not enforced below is disabled explicitly.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh
  # stage_size + the ci.yml shell guard). agent_service.dart and
  # wasm_shell.dart sit under 2800 today; the app_localizations*.dart
  # pattern covers ALL gen-l10n output (base + every locale variant —
  # en/ru today, future locales automatically): generated files no human
  # edits, excluded here, not baselined.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - 'lib/l10n/app_localizations*.dart'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet below already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  duplication: {enabled: false} # own jscpd <1% guard (global %) — 0.10.0's
    # `duplication.sources` cross-module key stays available if the jscpd
    # guards are ever retired (mirrors the root crap4dart.yaml)
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over the golden set (165 PNGs). severity: warning + the
  # excludes below are the documented INTERIM mitigation (#447): the
  # 0.9.5 detector knows only 3 shapes — it missed both classes that
  # broke the 40 pre-font goldens of de2f11b9 (solid Ahem text
  # rectangles, hollow icon squares without an X) and false-positives on:
  #   - the Habit Tracker checkmark tile (green square + white V
  #     converging like an X signature; light theme only, the same 22px
  #     tile at x=234 in all 5 hits),
  #   - the yellow "25:00" digits on the dark timer card (row y=195 of
  #     apps_panel/panel_dark: yellow glyph edges alternate with the
  #     dark card ≥8px with ≥4 transitions — passes the stripe
  #     heuristic).
  # Each exclude is an upstream IstiN/crap4dart bug. Flip to
  # `severity: error` and drop the excludes when the upstream detector
  # fixes land — scripts/check_golden_detector.py re-verifies all six
  # classes against this exact detector (see its docstring).
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test/golden/goldens]
    exclude:
      # false positives: green checkmark tile reads as an X (light theme)
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/grid_light.png'
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/sheet_bar_light.png'
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/sheet_bar_streaming_light.png…

blocks.text:
**Root cause of the CRAP gate failure:** `CRAP threshold exceeded: 90.00 > 30.0`.

Some function in `flutter_app` (per `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml` scope) has CRAP score 90 (max threshold 30). CRAP = comp+¹ × coverage-weighted. A CRAP of 90 means a complex, UNCOVERED function. My change touched only a test file — tests don't enter the crap scope (lib scope). The previous pass added code to `js_app_engine.dart` (`_containsVoxelNode` recursion, `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld`) and `apps_golden_test.dart`... but lib files are the scope.

Which function has CRAP 90? The CI ratchet doesn't name it in this tail — let me run crap4dart locally to find it. The CRAP gate measures coverage-weighted crap: the CI merges app-coverage shards and computes. My local run can reproduce: `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` needs the coverage lcov at flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info presumably.

Which function could be at 90? `_containsVoxelNode` in js_app_engine.dart — complexity: if/else-if, loops, recursion... CRAP = crap(comp, coverage) = comp² + comp×(1−coverage). If comp ~9 and coverage 0 → 90. comp 9 ≈ 8 decision points + 1. `_containsVoxelNode`: `depth > 64` (1), `is Map` (2), `== 'voxel'` (3), for loop (4), `is List` (5), for loop (6) → comp 7 → 7²=49+7×(1−cov). With cov 0 → 56. Hmm not 90.

`maskedForScan`? That's in ROOT test/ — flutter_app scope only covers flutter_app/lib. The 90 could be a function in flutter_app/lib with the merged coverage from the 2 shards. Wait — which functions did this PR add to flutter_app/lib? `voxelWorld` getter (comp 1), `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld` (comp ~5), `_containsVoxelNode` (comp 7). None hit 90 unless uncovered with higher comp.

Hold on — the CRAP ratchet compares against a BASELINE (`.crap-baseline.json` at repo root, `crap4dart.yaml` + `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`). "CRAP threshold exceeded: 90.00 > 30.0" — the gate reports the WORST offender. The ratchet baseline should hold known offenders. If a NEW function exceeded 30 (uncovered by the CI shards), the gate fails.

Key: the CI coverage shards come from "Flutter app tests (shard 0/2, 1/2)" — which run the full flutter_app test suite? If the coverage suite doesn't execute `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld`/`_containsVoxelNode` (engine-gated tests SKIP on bare ubuntu CI shards — "skip on bare ubuntu"!), those functions have ZERO coverage → CRAP = comp² + comp.

`_containsVoxelNode`: comp 7 → 49+7 = 56. Not 90. Unless I undercount decisions: `if (depth > 64) return false;` (1), `if (node is Map)` (2), `if (node['type'] == 'voxel')` (3), `for (final value in node.values)` (4), `else if (node is List)` (5), `for (...)` (6), `if (_containsVoxelNode(...)) return true` (7) → comp = 8 → 64+8 = 72. Still not 90.

# crap4dart configuration for the flutter_app package.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET (issue #433): the threshold is pinned at the CURRENT worst score
# measured by the SAME pipeline the CI gate uses — `flutter test --coverage`
# lcov (E2: widget-test coverage differs from the core's dart lcov, so the
# number must come from this pipeline, not the core's).
# Bootstrap (2026-09-15): 2450.0 — `JsAppEngine._faCall` (CC 49, 0% line
# coverage). Descent #1 (same day): the issue's three named offenders went
# under the next milestone line (CRAP ≤ 40 each) and the threshold followed
# the measured new worst: 2450.0 → 870.0 (`wasm_shell_git.run` and
# `main`, CC 29 at 0% coverage). Descent #2 (issue #475): both beasts
# decomposed into route-table dispatch + per-family handlers with a 51-test
# golden suite, and the cluster's own 812/702/600/506 beasts went down with
# them; the threshold follows the new measured worst: 870.0 → 650.0
# (`runCodemieSsoFlow`, CC 25 at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card).
# Descent #9 (issue #485): the on-device provider stream functions moved to
# one shared pump + codec walk (lib/on_device/), and the beasts went down
# with them — gemma 992 → 9, transformers.js 552/506 → 17/1, webllm 420 → 6
# (all fully covered by the provider suites + the new codec-table/pump
# tests); the threshold follows the measured new worst: 650.0 → 380.0
# (`WasiSandboxShell._runStage`, CC 19 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell cluster,
# another lane's ladder card).
# Pushes may only make the codebase BETTER,
# never worse; scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down rejects a raised
# threshold in CI. The staged ladder continues in follow-up cards:
# 870 → … → 40 (see AGENTS.md "Quality gates"). Re-measure after each fix:
# cd flutter_app && flutter test --coverage &&
# dart pub global run crap4dart analyze.

sources: [lib]

# Same generated set as the root config (E1 parity — asserted by
# scripts/check_crap_guards.py).
exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in flutter_app/lib under the flutter lcov
  # pipeline. Descent #10 (issue #558): the wasm_shell pipeline-engine
  # cluster went down (_runStage 380→4, _runPipeline 210→4, _evalExpr
  # 182→3, _rewriteRelativeArgs 110→2, _maybeRewritePath 72→3, all 100%
  # covered by test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows
  # the measured new worst: 380.0 → 272.0 (`WasiSandboxShell._xargsBuiltin`,
  # CC 16 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell builtins cluster, the next lane's
  # ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #11 (issue #559): the wasm_shell builtins cluster went down
  # (xargs 272→7, _parsePrimary 210→3, _testBuiltin 132→9, du 132→3,
  # tac 90→6, tr 25.9→4, pip 72→3, _expandTrSet 30.8→gone — table/spec
  # driven parse helpers now live in wasm_shell_builtins.dart with direct
  # unit tests, the exec halves are covered e2e in
  # test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows the
  # measured new worst: 272.0 → 210.0 (`GemmaService.chatStream`, CC 14
  # at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #12 (issue #701): the 0%-coverage trio went down (_statBuiltin
  # 156→12.1 @ 91% cov via test/wasm_shell_stat_test.dart, isFaCliInstalled
  # 110→6 via the extracted faCliProbe seam + test/sessions_root_test.dart,
  # _showAppMenu 90→9 @ 100% cov via test/apps/apps_panel_menu_test.dart);
  # the threshold follows the measured new worst: 210.0 → 30.0 (the CC-5
  # 0%-cov tier: routeExtHostMessage, codemie _createController, attached
  # _AttachedRow.build, GemmaService.loadModel — the next ladder cards).
  # Re-measured on the CI pipeline (app-crap-gate run 35479048998): local
  # lcov is impossible on the agent cube (the flutter coverage collector
  # canonicalizes source paths and lstat EPERMs through .worktrees). Only
  # down.
  # TEMP raise (owner call 2026-09-26, mirrors dmtools-dart #256): the #955
  # network-mode merge shipped widgets without tests — max CRAP 72.0
  # (_ChannelRailState._createChannel, CC 8 @ 0% cov). Restore to 30.0 via
  # the linked issue.
  # raise-issue: gh-992
  # Restored (gh-992, 2026-09-27): the agents/enroll DAP-tab rework
  # (fcd2d0232) covered the #955 network UI — 5 enroll dialog groups +
  # channel_rail/chat_page call-site suites, 72 focused tests; re-measured
  # on the full local flutter lcov (3292 green): max CRAP 30.0, the
  # threshold follows back down 75.0 → 30.0. Only down.
  threshold: 30.0

coverage:
  # The CI app-crap-gate job merges the two flutter-tests shard reports
  # (scripts/merge_lcov.py) right before the CRAP step. Pre-commit stays
  # core-only: flutter coverage is too heavy for every commit.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  # flutter's lcov carries no BRDA branch records; branch coverage stays
  # a core-package gate concern.
  branch_coverage: false
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole flutter suite
  # first. Coverage comes from the CI shard merge (scripts/merge_lcov.py)
  # and pre-commit stays core-only (#433 split); nobody wants a second
  # suite run inside a 6-minute gate job.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This config is the single source of which gates `crap4dart check` runs
# (CI app-crap-gate job, pre-commit core hook): 0.9.5 default-enables ALL
# built-in gates, so everything not enforced below is disabled explicitly.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh
  # stage_size + the ci.yml shell guard). agent_service.dart and
  # wasm_shell.dart sit under 2800 today; the app_localizations*.dart
  # pattern covers ALL gen-l10n output (base + every locale variant —
  # en/ru today, future locales automatically): generated files no human
  # edits, excluded here, not baselined.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - 'lib/l10n/app_localizations*.dart'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet below already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  duplication: {enabled: false} # own jscpd <1% guard (global %) — 0.10.0's
    # `duplication.sources` cross-module key stays available if the jscpd
    # guards are ever retired (mirrors the root crap4dart.yaml)
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over the golden set (165 PNGs). severity: warning + the
  # excludes below are the documented INTERIM mitigation (#447): the
  # 0.9.5 detector knows only 3 shapes — it missed both classes that
  # broke the 40 pre-font goldens of de2f11b9 (solid Ahem text
  # rectangles, hollow icon squares without an X) and false-positives on:
  #   - the Habit Tracker checkmark tile (green square + white V
  #     converging like an X signature; light theme only, the same 22px
  #     tile at x=234 in all 5 hits),
  #   - the yellow "25:00" digits on the dark timer card (row y=195 of
  #     apps_panel/panel_dark: yellow glyph edges alternate with the
  #     dark card ≥8px with ≥4 transitions — passes the stripe
  #     heuristic).
  # Each exclude is an upstream IstiN/crap4dart bug. Flip to
  # `severity: error` and drop the excludes when the upstream detector
  # fixes land — scripts/check_golden_detector.py re-verifies all six
  # classes against this exact detector (see its docstring).
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test/golden/goldens]
    exclude:
      # false positives: green checkmark tile reads as an X (light theme)
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/grid_light.png'
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/sheet_bar_light.png'

Which function could be at 90? `_containsVoxelNode` in js_app_engine.dart — complexity: if/else-if, loops, recursion... CRAP = crap(comp, coverage) = comp² + comp×(1−coverage). If comp ~9 and coverage 0 → 90. comp 9 ≈ 8 decision points + 1. `_containsVoxelNode`: `depth > 64` (1), `is Map` (2), `== 'voxel'` (3), for loop (4), `is List` (5), for loop (6) → comp 7 → 7²=49+7×(1−cov). blocks.text:
# crap4dart configuration for the flutter_app package.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET (issue #433): the threshold is pinned at the CURRENT worst score
# measured by the SAME pipeline the CI gate uses — `flutter test --coverage`
# lcov (E2: widget-test coverage differs from the core's dart lcov, so the
# number must come from this pipeline, not the core's).
# Bootstrap (2026-09-15): 2450.0 — `JsAppEngine._faCall` (CC 49, 0% line
# coverage). Descent #1 (same day): the issue's three named offenders went
# under the next milestone line (CRAP ≤ 40 each) and the threshold followed
# the measured new worst: 2450.0 → 870.0 (`wasm_shell_git.run` and
# `main`, CC 29 at 0% coverage). Descent #2 (issue #475): both beasts
# decomposed into route-table dispatch + per-family handlers with a 51-test
# golden suite, and the cluster's own 812/702/600/506 beasts went down with
# them; the threshold follows the new measured worst: 870.0 → 650.0
# (`runCodemieSsoFlow`, CC 25 at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card).
# Descent #9 (issue #485): the on-device provider stream functions moved to
# one shared pump + codec walk (lib/on_device/), and the beasts went down
# with them — gemma 992 → 9, transformers.js 552/506 → 17/1, webllm 420 → 6
# (all fully covered by the provider suites + the new codec-table/pump
# tests); the threshold follows the measured new worst: 650.0 → 380.0
# (`WasiSandboxShell._runStage`, CC 19 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell cluster,
# another lane's ladder card).
# Pushes may only make the codebase BETTER,
# never worse; scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down rejects a raised
# threshold in CI. The staged ladder continues in follow-up cards:
# 870 → … → 40 (see AGENTS.md "Quality gates"). Re-measure after each fix:
# cd flutter_app && flutter test --coverage &&
# dart pub global run crap4dart analyze.

sources: [lib]

# Same generated set as the root config (E1 parity — asserted by
# scripts/check_crap_guards.py).
exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in flutter_app/lib under the flutter lcov
  # pipeline. Descent #10 (issue #558): the wasm_shell pipeline-engine
  # cluster went down (_runStage 380→4, _runPipeline 210→4, _evalExpr
  # 182→3, _rewriteRelativeArgs 110→2, _maybeRewritePath 72→3, all 100%
  # covered by test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows
  # the measured new worst: 380.0 → 272.0 (`WasiSandboxShell._xargsBuiltin`,
  # CC 16 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell builtins cluster, the next lane's
  # ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #11 (issue #559): the wasm_shell builtins cluster went down
  # (xargs 272→7, _parsePrimary 210→3, _testBuiltin 132→9, du 132→3,
  # tac 90→6, tr 25.9→4, pip 72→3, _expandTrSet 30.8→gone — table/spec
  # driven parse helpers now live in wasm_shell_builtins.dart with direct
  # unit tests, the exec halves are covered e2e in
  # test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows the
  # measured new worst: 272.0 → 210.0 (`GemmaService.chatStream`, CC 14
  # at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #12 (issue #701): the 0%-coverage trio went down (_statBuiltin
  # 156→12.1 @ 91% cov via test/wasm_shell_stat_test.dart, isFaCliInstalled
  # 110→6 via the extracted faCliProbe seam + test/sessions_root_test.dart,
  # _showAppMenu 90→9 @ 100% cov via test/apps/apps_panel_menu_test.dart);
  # the threshold follows the measured new worst: 210.0 → 30.0 (the CC-5
  # 0%-cov tier: routeExtHostMessage, codemie _createController, attached
  # _AttachedRow.build, GemmaService.loadModel — the next ladder cards).
  # Re-measured on the CI pipeline (app-crap-gate run 35479048998): local
  # lcov is impossible on the agent cube (the flutter coverage collector
  # canonicalizes source paths and lstat EPERMs through .worktrees). Only
  # down.
  # TEMP raise (owner call 2026-09-26, mirrors dmtools-dart #256): the #955
  # network-mode merge shipped widgets without tests — max CRAP 72.0
  # (_ChannelRailState._createChannel, CC 8 @ 0% cov). Restore to 30.0 via
  # the linked issue.
  # raise-issue: gh-992
  # Restored (gh-992, 2026-09-27): the agents/enroll DAP-tab rework
  # (fcd2d0232) covered the #955 network UI — 5 enroll dialog groups +
  # channel_rail/chat_page call-site suites, 72 focused tests; re-measured
  # on the full local flutter lcov (3292 green): max CRAP 30.0, the
  # threshold follows back down 75.0 → 30.0. Only down.
  threshold: 30.0

coverage:
  # The CI app-crap-gate job merges the two flutter-tests shard reports
  # (scripts/merge_lcov.py) right before the CRAP step. Pre-commit stays
  # core-only: flutter coverage is too heavy for every commit.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  # flutter's lcov carries no BRDA branch records; branch coverage stays
  # a core-package gate concern.
  branch_coverage: false
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole flutter suite
  # first. Coverage comes from the CI shard merge (scripts/merge_lcov.py)
  # and pre-commit stays core-only (#433 split); nobody wants a second
  # suite run inside a 6-minute gate job.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This config is the single source of which gates `crap4dart check` runs
# (CI app-crap-gate job, pre-commit core hook): 0.9.5 default-enables ALL
# built-in gates, so everything not enforced below is disabled explicitly.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh
  # stage_size + the ci.yml shell guard). agent_service.dart and
  # wasm_shell.dart sit under 2800 today; the app_localizations*.dart
  # pattern covers ALL gen-l10n output (base + every locale variant —
  # en/ru today, future locales automatically): generated files no human
  # edits, excluded here, not baselined.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - 'lib/l10n/app_localizations*.dart'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet below already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  duplication: {enabled: false} # own jscpd <1% guard (global %) — 0.10.0's
    # `duplication.sources` cross-module key stays available if the jscpd
    # guards are ever retired (mirrors the root crap4dart.yaml)
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over the golden set (165 PNGs). severity: warning + the
  # excludes below are the documented INTERIM mitigation (#447): the
  # 0.9.5 detector knows only 3 shapes — it missed both classes that
  # broke the 40 pre-font goldens of de2f11b9 (solid Ahem text
  # rectangles, hollow icon squares without an X) and false-positives on:
  #   - the Habit Tracker checkmark tile (green square + white V
  #     converging like an X signature; light theme only, the same 22px
  #     tile at x=234 in all 5 hits),
  #   - the yellow "25:00" digits on the dark timer card (row y=195 of
  #     apps_panel/panel_dark: yellow glyph edges alternate with the
  #     dark card ≥8px with ≥4 transitions — passes the stripe
  #     heuristic).
  # Each exclude is an upstream IstiN/crap4dart bug. Flip to
  # `severity: error` and drop the excludes when the upstream detector
  # fixes land — scripts/check_golden_detector.py re-verifies all six
  # classes against this exact detector (see its docstring).
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test/golden/goldens]
    exclude:
      # false positives: green checkmark tile reads as an X (light theme)
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/grid_light.png'
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/sheet_bar_light.png'
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/sheet_bar_streaming_light.png…

The check-suite containing those three "failing" check-runs has **conclusion: success** — the suite-level verdict is green (each check-run inside can be individually marked failure while the suite succeeded? Actually suite conclusion derives from its check-runs... odd, but that's what the API says). These three check-runs started at 18:53:05 — created by some external process (likely the dmtools/rework SM) that re-posted job status summaries to the PR as check-runs; the suite aggregates to success. They are NOT required CI jobs — the real failed CI leg is the CRAP ratchet (via the Quality gate aggregate).

Conclusion: **the single real CI root cause = flutter_app CRAP 90 (`_containsVoxelNode`, CC 9, 0% cov) > threshold 30.** Fix that and CI goes green (CI re-runs automatically on push).

Also worth noting: the ci_failures.md list is partly a red herring (stale/duplicate check-runs), but the actionable root cause stands. I'll note this in the response.

Now implement:

1. **Fix `_containsVoxelNode`** — idiomatic `.any()` form (CC 5), behavior identical.

2. **TDD:** the "failing test" here is the CI gate itself. I can reproduce the gate locally EXACTLY: download app-coverage shard artifacts, merge via scripts/merge_lcov.py, run crap4dart 0.11.0 analyze → maxCrap 90 (RED, matches CI), apply fix → maxCrap ≤30 (GREEN). That's a faithful RED→GREEN on the real pipeline.

3. **Regression test for the semantics** (the .any rewrite must not change behavior): the helper is private; behavior is observable via `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld` + AppLog — but only reachable with a live null-world engine (not constructible). Hmm. However there IS a directly callable surface: `JsAppEngine._containsVoxelNode` is private. No test seam. Options: make it `@visibleForTesting` public-ish? The repo pattern: `uiTreeWarnAfter` is `@visibleForTesting static`. I could expose `@visibleForTesting static bool containsVoxelNodeForTest(Object? node)`... Modifying lib API for tests — AGENTS.md says "never by extracting public API" (that's about splitting god files). A `@visibleForTesting` static delegate is a small, established seam (the file already has two `@visibleForTesting` members). It lets me unit-test the recursion DIRECTLY: deep nesting, lists, maps, depth cap, non-voxel scalars — all on any host, covering most branches (NOT the recursion... no wait, direct unit tests DO cover all branches: nested lists, maps, depth cap). That gives `_containsVoxelNode` REAL coverage on the CI ubuntu shards (the shard suite runs test/apps widget tests — a plain `testWidgets`/`test` in the engine test file runs on ubuntu without the bridge) → coverage ↑ AND CRAP ↓↓. 

That's the complete honest fix:
- seam: `@visibleForTesting static bool containsVoxelNode(Object? node) => _containsVoxelNode(node, depth: 0);` — hmm, or rename: keep private impl, add visible-for-testing wrapper. 
- tests: direct unit pins for the tree walk (voxel in map, voxel in nested list, voxel deep, depth cap 64 → false for >64 nesting, empty/scalar false, cyclic? JSON decode never cyclic — skip).
- complexity: rewrite with `.any()`.

Wait — with real unit coverage, do I even NEED the CC reduction? Covered CC 9 → CRAP = 81×cov-factor... crap formula: comp² × (1-cov) + comp. Fully covered (cov=1) → CRAP = comp = 9 < 30. Partial coverage: CRAP = comp² + comp(1−cov) → at 50%: 81+4.5 = 85.5 — still >30! So coverage must be ~100% to get under 30 with CC 9. My unit tests can reach 100% line coverage of the helper EASILY on any host (direct calls hit every branch incl. depth cap). But if the CI shard suite doesn't run that test file... it does — the non-engine tests in js_app_engine_voxel_world_test.dart already RUN on ubuntu (they passed in CI presumably: "Flutter app tests" shards green, and the boot-gap/disposed tests are not bridge-gated).

Risk of relying on coverage alone: lcov line-coverage for the helper must hit EVERY line (the two `for` bodies, both returns). My unit tests can do that deterministically. But the CI gate measured 0.0% — because no test reached it. With direct unit tests, coverage lands on the shards → CRAP 9. 

Belt and braces: do BOTH (CC ≤5 via `.any()` AND the direct unit tests). Then even if some line stays unhit on CI (e.g. depth-cap line), worst CRAP = 25+5×(1−cov) ≤ 30 — hmm, uncovered `depth>64` branch: lines hit = all except one → lcov line coverage ~ 11/12 → CRAP = 25 + 5×(1−0.92) ≈ 25.4 < 30. Robust either way. 

4. **Guard suggestion thread (index 4)** — implement the two scanner hardenings in test/jsr_voxel_world_pin_guard_test.dart:
   a. Strip nested balanced `(...)` groups from captured args before the `voxelWorld:` `contains` (closes the nested-call false GREEN).
   b. Track `${...}` interpolation nesting in `maskedForScan` (string interpolation: `'${a['k']}'` — treat `${` inside a string as entering code context until the matching `}`). 

   Both TDD-able with scanner unit pins (the file already has the harness). RED: write pins that fail against the current scanner (e.g. `JsonWidgetRenderer(theme: resolve(voxelWorld: w))` must NOT pass the per-site check → the pin asserts the masked+stripped args do NOT contain voxelWorld; currently the raw contains() says it does → pin fails → then implement stripping). For interpolation: a pin where a `'${x}'` string containing `)` previously desynced balancedArgs.

   Hmm — how does the guard test assert per-site "voxelWorld in the CONSTRUCTION's own args" vs nested? New helper `topLevelArgs(maskedArgs)` that strips nested balanced groups; the main guard test uses it for the `contains('voxelWorld:')` assertion. Pins in the hardening group prove: nested-call shape → stripped args lack voxelWorld → treated as UNWIRED (RED direction for a real site) — wait, careful: the guard's assertion is `expect(args, contains('voxelWorld:'))` for every site — if a site had ONLY a nested voxelWorld, stripped args lack it → guard RED (correct: the construction omits the param). The pin: `rendererConstructionsOf` on `final r = JsonWidgetRenderer(theme: resolve(voxelWorld: w));` → stripped args must NOT contain 'voxelWorld:' → the guard would flag it. Assert `topLevelArgsOnly(args)` doesn't contain it while raw args do — pins the new behavior.

blocks.text:
**Root cause of the CRAP gate failure:** `CRAP threshold exceeded: 90.00 > 30.0`.

Some function in `flutter_app` (per `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml` scope) has CRAP score 90 (max threshold 30). CRAP = comp+¹ × coverage-weighted. A CRAP of 90 means a complex, UNCOVERED function. My change touched only a test file — tests don't enter the crap scope (lib scope). The previous pass added code to `js_app_engine.dart` (`_containsVoxelNode` recursion, `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld`) and `apps_golden_test.dart`... but lib files are the scope.

Which function has CRAP 90? The CI ratchet doesn't name it in this tail — let me run crap4dart locally to find it. The CRAP gate measures coverage-weighted crap: the CI merges app-coverage shards and computes. My local run can reproduce: `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` needs the coverage lcov at flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info presumably.

Which function could be at 90? `_containsVoxelNode` in js_app_engine.dart — complexity: if/else-if, loops, recursion... CRAP = crap(comp, coverage) = comp² + comp×(1−coverage). blocks.text:
**Root cause of the CRAP gate failure:** `CRAP threshold exceeded: 90.00 > 30.0`.

Some function in `flutter_app` (per `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml` scope) has CRAP score 90 (max threshold 30). CRAP = comp+¹ × coverage-weighted. A CRAP of 90 means a complex, UNCOVERED function. My change touched only a test file — tests don't enter the crap scope (lib scope). The previous pass added code to `js_app_engine.dart` (`_containsVoxelNode` recursion, `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld`) and `apps_golden_test.dart`... but lib files are the scope.

Which function has CRAP 90? The CI ratchet doesn't name it in this tail — let me run crap4dart locally to find it. The CRAP gate measures coverage-weighted crap: the CI merges app-coverage shards and computes. My local run can reproduce: `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` needs the coverage lcov at flutter_app/coverage/lcov.info presumably.

Which function could be at 90? `_containsVoxelNode` in js_app_engine.dart — complexity: if/else-if, loops, recursion... CRAP = crap(comp, coverage) = comp² + comp×(1−coverage). If comp ~9 and coverage 0 → 90. comp 9 ≈ 8 decision points + 1. `_containsVoxelNode`: `depth > 64` (1), `is Map` (2), `== 'voxel'` (3), for loop (4), `is List` (5), for loop (6) → comp 7 → 7²=49+7×(1−cov). With cov 0 → 56. Hmm not 90.

`maskedForScan`? That's in ROOT test/ — flutter_app scope only covers flutter_app/lib. The 90 could be a function in flutter_app/lib with the merged coverage from the 2 shards. Wait — which functions did this PR add to flutter_app/lib? `voxelWorld` getter (comp 1), `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld` (comp ~5), `_containsVoxelNode` (comp 7). None hit 90 unless uncovered with higher comp.

Hold on — the CRAP ratchet compares against a BASELINE (`.crap-baseline.json` at repo root, `crap4dart.yaml` + `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`). "CRAP threshold exceeded: 90.00 > 30.0" — the gate reports the WORST offender. The ratchet baseline should hold known offenders. If a NEW function exceeded 30 (uncovered by the CI shards), the gate fails.

Key: the CI coverage shards come from "Flutter app tests (shard 0/2, 1/2)" — which run the full flutter_app test suite? If the coverage suite doesn't execute `noteUnwiredVoxelWorld`/`_containsVoxelNode` (engine-gated tests SKIP on bare ubuntu CI shards — "skip on bare ubuntu"!), those functions have ZERO coverage → CRAP = comp² + comp.

`_containsVoxelNode`: comp 7 → 49+7 = 56. Not 90. Unless I undercount decisions: `if (depth > 64) return false;` (1), `if (node is Map)` (2), `if (node['type'] == 'voxel')` (3), `for (final value in node.values)` (4), `else if (node is List)` (5), `for (...)` (6), `if (_containsVoxelNode(...)) return true` (7) → comp = 8 → 64+8 = 72. Still not 90.

`noteUnwiredVoxelWorld`: `if (_unwiredVoxelNoted || engine == null || engine.voxelWorld != null)` — || counts as decisions: 3, + `if (!_containsVoxelNode(tree...))` 4 → comp 5 → 30 uncovered. Under 30? comp 5 → 25+5 = 30 → "30.0 > 30.0" false. Hmm.

What about the golden test's `addVoxel`? It's in test/ — not in scope (flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml scope is probably flutter_app/lib; and the loc-scope companion covers test/example for LOC only).

Wait — maybe the CRAP 90 offender is NOT from this PR at all. The merge with main brought new code. The baseline `.crap-baseline.json` at repo root — maybe the branch's merge with main updated lib code beyond the baseline. OR the PR's earlier commits (the previous agent's) added something with comp 9 uncovered: e.g., `maskedForScan` is in ROOT test/. Hmm.

Actually — wait. Let me reconsider: maybe the crap gate failure is NOT caused by this PR's code but by the merged main + the ratchet's baseline. The ratchet would have caught it on main too... unless the merge combined changes. Let me just run the gate locally and find the offender. The repo has crap4dart configs. Run:

```

Which function could be at 90? `_containsVoxelNode` in js_app_engine.dart — complexity: if/else-if, loops, recursion... CRAP = crap(comp, coverage) = comp² + comp×(1−coverage). If comp ~9 and coverage 0 → 90. comp 9 ≈ 8 decision points + 1. `_containsVoxelNode`: `depth > 64` (1), `is Map` (2), `== 'voxel'` (3), for loop (4), `is List` (5), for loop (6) → comp 7 → 7²=49+7×(1−cov). # crap4dart configuration for the flutter_app package.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET (issue #433): the threshold is pinned at the CURRENT worst score
# measured by the SAME pipeline…

blocks.text:
# crap4dart configuration for the flutter_app package.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET (issue #433): the threshold is pinned at the CURRENT worst score
# measured by the SAME pipeline the CI gate uses — `flutter test --coverage`
# lcov (E2: widget-test coverage differs from the core's dart lcov, so the
# number must come from this pipeline, not the core's).
# Bootstrap (2026-09-15): 2450.0 — `JsAppEngine._faCall` (CC 49, 0% line
# coverage). Descent #1 (same day): the issue's three named offenders went
# under the next milestone line (CRAP ≤ 40 each) and the threshold followed
# the measured new worst: 2450.0 → 870.0 (`wasm_shell_git.run` and
# `main`, CC 29 at 0% coverage). Descent #2 (issue #475): both beasts
# decomposed into route-table dispatch + per-family handlers with a 51-test
# golden suite, and the cluster's own 812/702/600/506 beasts went down with
# them; the threshold follows the new measured worst: 870.0 → 650.0
# (`runCodemieSsoFlow`, CC 25 at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card).
# Descent #9 (issue #485): the on-device provider stream functions moved to
# one shared pump + codec walk (lib/on_device/), and the beasts went down
# with them — gemma 992 → 9, transformers.js 552/506 → 17/1, webllm 420 → 6
# (all fully covered by the provider suites + the new codec-table/pump
# tests); the threshold follows the measured new worst: 650.0 → 380.0
# (`WasiSandboxShell._runStage`, CC 19 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell cluster,
# another lane's ladder card).
# Pushes may only make the codebase BETTER,
# never worse; scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down rejects a raised
# threshold in CI. The staged ladder continues in follow-up cards:
# 870 → … → 40 (see AGENTS.md "Quality gates"). Re-measure after each fix:
# cd flutter_app && flutter test --coverage &&
# dart pub global run crap4dart analyze.

sources: [lib]

# Same generated set as the root config (E1 parity — asserted by
# scripts/check_crap_guards.py).
exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in flutter_app/lib under the flutter lcov
  # pipeline. Descent #10 (issue #558): the wasm_shell pipeline-engine
  # cluster went down (_runStage 380→4, _runPipeline 210→4, _evalExpr
  # 182→3, _rewriteRelativeArgs 110→2, _maybeRewritePath 72→3, all 100%
  # covered by test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows
  # the measured new worst: 380.0 → 272.0 (`WasiSandboxShell._xargsBuiltin`,
  # CC 16 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell builtins cluster, the next lane's
  # ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #11 (issue #559): the wasm_shell builtins cluster went down
  # (xargs 272→7, _parsePrimary 210→3, _testBuiltin 132→9, du 132→3,
  # tac 90→6, tr 25.9→4, pip 72→3, _expandTrSet 30.8→gone — table/spec
  # driven parse helpers now live in wasm_shell_builtins.dart with direct
  # unit tests, the exec halves are covered e2e in
  # test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows the
  # measured new worst: 272.0 → 210.0 (`GemmaService.chatStream`, CC 14
  # at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #12 (issue #701): the 0%-coverage trio went down (_statBuiltin
  # 156→12.1 @ 91% cov via test/wasm_shell_stat_test.dart, isFaCliInstalled
  # 110→6 via the extracted faCliProbe seam + test/sessions_root_test.dart,
  # _showAppMenu 90→9 @ 100% cov via test/apps/apps_panel_menu_test.dart);
  # the threshold follows the measured new worst: 210.0 → 30.0 (the CC-5
  # 0%-cov tier: routeExtHostMessage, codemie _createController, attached
  # _AttachedRow.build, GemmaService.loadModel — the next ladder cards).
  # Re-measured on the CI pipeline (app-crap-gate run 35479048998): local
  # lcov is impossible on the agent cube (the flutter coverage collector
  # canonicalizes source paths and lstat EPERMs through .worktrees). Only
  # down.
  # TEMP raise (owner call 2026-09-26, mirrors dmtools-dart #256): the #955
  # network-mode merge shipped widgets without tests — max CRAP 72.0
  # (_ChannelRailState._createChannel, CC 8 @ 0% cov). Restore to 30.0 via
  # the linked issue.
  # raise-issue: gh-992
  # Restored (gh-992, 2026-09-27): the agents/enroll DAP-tab rework
  # (fcd2d0232) covered the #955 network UI — 5 enroll dialog groups +
  # channel_rail/chat_page call-site suites, 72 focused tests; re-measured
  # on the full local flutter lcov (3292 green): max CRAP 30.0, the
  # threshold follows back down 75.0 → 30.0. Only down.
  threshold: 30.0

coverage:
  # The CI app-crap-gate job merges the two flutter-tests shard reports
  # (scripts/merge_lcov.py) right before the CRAP step. Pre-commit stays
  # core-only: flutter coverage is too heavy for every commit.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  # flutter's lcov carries no BRDA branch records; branch coverage stays
  # a core-package gate concern.
  branch_coverage: false
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole flutter suite
  # first. Coverage comes from the CI shard merge (scripts/merge_lcov.py)
  # and pre-commit stays core-only (#433 split); nobody wants a second
  # suite run inside a 6-minute gate job.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This config is the single source of which gates `crap4dart check` runs
# (CI app-crap-gate job, pre-commit core hook): 0.9.5 default-enables ALL
# built-in gates, so everything not enforced below is disabled explicitly.
gates:
  # Issue #1234: whole-tree ≤2800-line guard (was scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh
  # stage_size + the ci.yml shell guard). agent_service.dart and
  # wasm_shell.dart sit under 2800 today; the app_localizations*.dart
  # pattern covers ALL gen-l10n output (base + every locale variant —
  # en/ru today, future locales automatically): generated files no human
  # edits, excluded here, not baselined.
  loc:
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 2800
    exclude:
      - 'lib/l10n/app_localizations*.dart'
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet below already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  duplication: {enabled: false} # own jscpd <1% guard (global %) — 0.10.0's
    # `duplication.sources` cross-module key stays available if the jscpd
    # guards are ever retired (mirrors the root crap4dart.yaml)
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over the golden set (165 PNGs). severity: warning + the
  # excludes below are the documented INTERIM mitigation (#447): the
  # 0.9.5 detector knows only 3 shapes — it missed both classes that
  # broke the 40 pre-font goldens of de2f11b9 (solid Ahem text
